nodes.name: Film Theory
nodes.description: The systematic study of the nature, function, and meaning of cinema.

nodes.name: Film History
nodes.description: The study of cinema's development across periods and nations.

nodes.name: Film Criticism
nodes.description: The evaluation and interpretation of films in journalism and scholarship.

nodes.name: Film Analysis
nodes.description: The close study of a film's style, structure, and meaning.

nodes.name: Film Genre Studies
nodes.description: The study of film genres, their conventions, and their cultural functions.

nodes.name: National Cinemas
nodes.description: The study of cinema organized by nation and filmmaking culture.

nodes.name: Documentary Studies
nodes.description: The study of documentary film, its forms, ethics, and truth claims.

nodes.name: Animation Studies
nodes.description: The study of animation, its techniques, and its cultural forms.

nodes.name: Film Aesthetics
nodes.description: The study of cinema's visual and sonic artistry and technique.

nodes.name: Film Industry Studies
nodes.description: The study of the production, distribution, and economics of cinema.

nodes.name: Auteur Theory
nodes.description: The theory that a film reflects the creative vision of its director.

nodes.name: Formalism
nodes.description: The theory emphasizing film's formal devices over its recorded reality.

nodes.name: Realism Theory
nodes.description: The theory emphasizing cinema's capacity to reveal reality.

nodes.name: Psychoanalytic Film Theory
nodes.description: The theory reading film through the unconscious, desire, and spectatorship.

nodes.name: Feminist Film Theory
nodes.description: The theory analyzing gender, the gaze, and representation in cinema.

nodes.name: Cognitive Film Theory
nodes.description: The theory explaining film spectatorship through cognitive processes.

nodes.name: Silent Film
nodes.description: The cinema of the pre-sound era before the late 1920s.

nodes.name: Classical Hollywood Cinema
nodes.description: The studio-era style of continuity editing and genre storytelling.

nodes.name: Italian Neorealism
nodes.description: The post-war Italian movement filming ordinary life with non-professional actors.

nodes.name: French New Wave
nodes.description: The late 1950s-60s French movement of young, self-reflexive auteurs.

nodes.name: Soviet Montage
nodes.description: The 1920s Soviet movement developing editing as the essence of cinema.

nodes.name: New German Cinema
nodes.description: The 1960s-70s West German movement of politically engaged auteurs.

nodes.name: Mise-en-Scene Analysis
nodes.description: The analysis of everything placed before the camera within a shot.

nodes.name: Western
nodes.description: The film genre set on the American frontier.

nodes.name: Film Noir
nodes.description: The dark, fatalistic crime cinema of 1940s-50s America.

nodes.name: Horror Film
nodes.description: The genre designed to frighten through the monstrous and uncanny.

nodes.name: Science Fiction Film
nodes.description: The genre imagining technological futures and speculative worlds.

nodes.name: Musical Film
nodes.description: The genre integrating song and dance into narrative.

nodes.name: Hollywood Cinema
nodes.description: The dominant American film industry and its global style.

nodes.name: French Cinema
nodes.description: The film tradition of France, from the Lumiere brothers onward.

nodes.name: Italian Cinema
nodes.description: The film tradition of Italy, from neorealism to the present.

nodes.name: German Cinema
nodes.description: The film tradition of Germany, from expressionism to the present.

nodes.name: Soviet and Russian Cinema
nodes.description: The film tradition of the Soviet Union and post-Soviet Russia.

nodes.name: Japanese Cinema
nodes.description: The film tradition of Japan, including its classical masters.

nodes.name: Chinese Cinema
nodes.description: The film tradition of mainland China across its political periods.

nodes.name: Hong Kong Cinema
nodes.description: The action and genre cinema of Hong Kong.

nodes.name: Indian Cinema
nodes.description: The diverse film industries of India, including Bollywood.

nodes.name: Iranian Cinema
nodes.description: The acclaimed art cinema of Iran.

nodes.name: Korean Cinema
nodes.description: The film tradition of South Korea.

nodes.name: Latin American Cinema
nodes.description: The film traditions of Latin America, including Third Cinema.

nodes.name: African Cinema
nodes.description: The film traditions of Africa, including Nollywood.

nodes.name: Observational Documentary
nodes.description: The documentary mode recording events without overt intervention.

nodes.name: Essay Film
nodes.description: The reflexive film form of personal reflection and argument.

nodes.name: Anime Studies
nodes.description: The study of Japanese animation and its global cultures.

nodes.name: Cinematography
nodes.description: The art and craft of camera, lighting, and visual composition.

nodes.name: Film Editing
nodes.description: The art of assembling shots into a coherent whole.

nodes.name: Film Sound
nodes.description: The study of sound design, music, and voice in cinema.
